Wave conditions

Local wave model
Checking local helper…

The local helper transforms the selected wave rows from their wave-stats location to the seawall toe.

100 means 100 × Tp after a 20 × Tp spin-up. This is approximately 100 irregular waves, not an exact wave count. JONSWAP γ = 3.3 and a repeatable seed are used. SWASH recommends 100–300 × Tp; up to 1000 × Tp is supported but can be much slower.

Only this final window is retained across the profile. It is stored as a compressed file in the model run folder and loaded by the viewer on demand.

Runs XBeach in 1D surfbeat mode after a 20 × Tp spin-up. The boundary is an irregular JONSWAP spectrum with γ = 3.3 and a repeatable seed. 1000 × Tp matches the requested physical-model wave count, but this is a duration rather than an exact count of individually resolved short waves.

Tick the required rows under Wave conditions, then run them locally. This stage returns toe Hm0, Tp, Tm−1,0, depth and setup; overtopping remains a separate EurOtop stage.

Export & share

Save the current setup, then load it in another copy of this HTML viewer.

Add the bathymetry to your existing flume drawing
  1. Open the exported DXF in AutoCAD.
  2. Select the bathymetry objects.
  3. Run COPYBASE.
  4. Enter base point 0,0.
  5. Switch to your existing flume drawing.
  6. Run PASTEORIG.

The DXF uses model millimetres and always includes separate bathy, batter-slope, and horizontal-extension layers.

Quick help
